title: The finite-stage boundary duality input
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$,
a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$
and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\ge1$, and put
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$
[def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type
$k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
Work on the small pro-etale sites with constant coefficient sheaves $A_T$;
$D^b_c(T,A)$ and its finite-Tor subcategory $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ are those of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
Use the derived pullback, tensor and internal Hom of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], writing $i^*$ for the exact
constant-coefficient pullback $Li^*$. A locally closed piece $T\subseteq Y$
means a subscheme given by an immersion into $Y$
[def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for its
structure morphism, and use the exceptional inverse images of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Their composition comparison for
composable separated finite-type $k$-morphisms $f,g$ is the natural
isomorphism $R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$ on bounded-below inputs: the
right-adjoint mate [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] of the etale
compact-support composition $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ on $D^+$
[lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] for the etale adjoints of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], transported along the unit isomorphism
$\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_*\nu^*$ on $D^+$ of
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. In particular, for a closed immersion
$i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with $a_Z=a_T\circ i$ it gives the identification
$Ri^!\omega_T\cong\omega_Z$ used below. The *boundary duality input* for
$(Y,A)$ consists of the following assertions, on the chosen finite-stage
coefficient categories.

1. For every locally closed $T\subseteq Y$, the exceptional
adjoints and their composition laws define
$\omega_T=Ra_T^!A$ and
$D_T=R\mathcal Hom_T(-,\omega_T)$, and $D_T$ carries
$D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ into itself.
1. For every closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ between such
pieces, the canonical boundary exchange
$$
\beta_L:i^*D_TL\longrightarrow D_ZRi^!L
\qquad(L\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A))
$$
is an isomorphism. It is the adjoint of the pairing
$$
i^*D_TL\otimes^L Ri^!L\longrightarrow
Ri^!(D_TL\otimes^L L)\longrightarrow Ri^!\omega_T=\omega_Z.
$$
For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ these comparisons are compatible with
the evaluation and double-dual morphism $\delta$ of
[lem-weil-duality-pairing]. More explicitly, let
$\alpha_K:Ri^!D_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Zi^*K$ be the canonical
adjunction comparison of [lem-weil-closed-costalk-duality]. Its
normalization is the tensor-Hom transpose of the pairing
$$
Ri^!D_TK\otimes^L i^*K
\xrightarrow{\sigma}i^*K\otimes^L Ri^!D_TK
\longrightarrow Ri^!(K\otimes^L D_TK)
\xrightarrow{Ri^!(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma)}\omega_Z,
$$
where $\sigma$ is tensor symmetry and the middle arrow is the same
canonical tensor-exceptional comparison used to define $\beta$ above.
The required compatibility is the equality of maps
$i^*K\to D_ZRi^!D_TK$,
$$
\beta_{D_TK}\circ i^*\delta_K
=D_Z(\alpha_K)\circ\delta_{i^*K}.
$$
Equivalently, composing the left hand side with
$(D_Z\alpha_K)^{-1}$ gives $\delta_{i^*K}$.

The first clause includes preservation of $D^b_{ctf}$ as a separate
condition. The second clause interchanges ordinary and exceptional
restriction; it does not identify $i^*$ with $Ri^!$.

split_report.summary: Second reading confirms a definition of a boundary-duality input, not an assertion of its existence: no proof steps or new nodes. Retained both blueprint clauses; expanded coefficient, site, scheme, operation and finite-Tor conventions using existing definition nodes, and wrote the typed evaluation-compatibility equation and canonical normalization of alpha. Preservation remains a condition in this record; cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge is the separate theorem establishing it. No exact Lean attachment or Mathlib match.

No SGA is cited. Setting and coefficient category match the source: k = algebraic closure of F_q, l != p, A = A_{E,n} with n >= 1, small pro-etale sites, D^b_c from def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, D^b_ctf from def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude. Clause 1 keeps preservation as a separate condition. Clause 2 type-checks; the finite-Tor condition is needed because A_{E,n} has infinite global dimension for n >= 2. In the expanded compatibility both sides are maps i^*K -> D_Z Ri^! D_T K. Transposing to pairings shows the equation holds with the stated normalization of alpha, and that normalization is the r_K the discharge constructs in steps 3 and 7. Small cases checked: zero objects, Z=T, Z empty, and T=Spec k with n=1. No new nodes, so B and D are vacuous; no duplicate found; the empty proof is correct for a definition. This gives Ri^! omega_T = omega_Z, as discharge step 0 does. The four ids were added to stmt_deps and none of them reaches the item, so no cycle.
